mechanism_name: London-morning -> New-York-overlap intraday continuation (session momentum, threshold-free, flat before NY rollover)

economic_mechanism.summary: FX information diffusion and order-flow imbalance are concentrated in the London-morning-to-NY-overlap window, the documented global activity peak of the FX day (Andersen & Bollerslev 1997). Intraday momentum - early-session directional moves persisting into the late session - is documented in US equity index futures (Gao, Han, Li & Zhou 2018: the first half-hour predicts the last half-hour). This proposal transfers the pattern one step earlier in the FX day: a directional move accumulated over the London morning (08:00-11:00 London completed bars) predicts continuation through the London afternoon and NY-morning overlap. The trade enters at 07:00 NY-equivalent, exits at the 15:00 NY flatten, and never holds any position into the 17:00 NY rollover.
economic_mechanism.profit_source: persistence of order-flow imbalance during the highest-liquidity, highest-information window of the FX day; macro releases at 08:30 America/New_York land inside the holding window and reinforce the morning direction on trend days
economic_mechanism.loss_source: overlap-ending mean reversion and profit-taking flow into the NY afternoon; range days where the morning move is the day's full excursion
economic_mechanism.why_threshold_free: the anchor has zero free parameters: every valid day trades the sign of the London-morning move. No filter level exists to tune; the mechanism either survives frozen conservative costs or is falsified
economic_mechanism.why_h1_bars_suffice: the signal is a 4-hour cumulative completed-bar return; the mechanism is a session-scale flow phenomenon, not a tick-level event
economic_mechanism.no_volume_claim: prices only; decentralized FX volume is never used

expected_counterparty.on_winning_trades: dealers and fast cross-market accounts still repositioning into the NY overlap; hedgers behind the morning imbalance (option rebalancing, reserve-manager flow) whose demand spans several hours
expected_counterparty.on_losing_trades: late-overlap liquidity providers who fade the morning extension once NY-morning flow peaks (profit-taking into the NY afternoon); on range days, the entire morning direction reverses and they are our counterparty at our 15:00 NY exit
expected_counterparty.why_they_let_us_win: the morning imbalance is information- and flow-driven and takes hours to diffuse; participants who cannot trade the morning (timezone-constrained hedgers, slower funds) transact into the overlap, continuing the move

signal_fields: twelvedata H1 close, UTC-stamped, completed canonical bars only (bar datetime = bar OPEN instant; actionable only at completion instant = open + 1h)
signal_fields_and_publication_clock.publication_clock: signal computed once, at the completion instant of the bar stamped 11:00 Europe/London (the last bar of the 4-bar signal window); never revised; fill at the next allowed bar open (12:00 London stamp)
signal_fields_and_publication_clock.session_labels: signal window keyed to Europe/London wall clock (UK DST via zoneinfo); exit/flatten keyed to America/New_York wall clock (US DST via zoneinfo); control arm keyed to Asia/Tokyo wall clock (no DST)

entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.signal_completed_bars_only: R = close(bar stamped 11:00 Europe/London) - close(bar stamped 07:00 Europe/London): the cumulative return of the 4 completed H1 bars stamped 08,09,10,11 London. Requires all 4 bars canonical and in-calendar (true every Mon-Fri; London 07:00-11:00 always follows the Sunday 21:00 NY weekly open). Otherwise no trade that day.
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.direction: sign(R); magnitude threshold NONE (zero free parameters); R = 0 -> no trade that day
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.entry_execution: fill at the open of the next allowed bar after the 11:00-London bar completes (the 12:00-London-stamped bar, ~07:00 NY-equivalent), provided that open maps to a NY wall-clock time strictly before 15:00 America/New_York; otherwise the signal is discarded
exits: mandatory flatten: every position exits with fill at the open of the H1 bar stamped 15:00 America/New_York (completion 16:00 NY, two full hours strictly before the 17:00 NY rollover instant); this is the ONLY exit - no stop, no target; identical rule on Friday where the 15:00 NY bar is the last bar of the week (frozen weekly close Fri 16:00 NY)

data-gap fail-conservative rule: if a fill bar is missing for an entry the order is cancelled; a missing exit bar defers the exit to the first available later bar open and is logged as a data-gap breach for A7 reconciliation - an exit later than the 15:00 NY boundary is never silently accepted
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.rollover_flat_invariant: no fill may execute at a bar open at or after 15:00 America/New_York; the book is flat from 15:00 NY wall clock, strictly before every 17:00 NY rollover under any bar-stamping convention; no position ever spans a rollover instant or the weekend; financing exposure zero by construction
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule.one_position_rule: at most one position per NY trading day; direction from sign(R) only

execution_model.fills: always at the OPEN price of the next allowed canonical bar; market-order semantics; no limit orders, no partial fills, no intrabar path assumptions
execution_model.allowed_bar: canonical deduped H1 bar of the frozen trading-week calendar (Sun 21:00 America/New_York -> Fri 16:00 close, DST-correct via zoneinfo); the canonical series contains no weekend bars
execution_model.no_assumptions: no bid/ask (proxy spread exists only inside the frozen cost stress), no volume, no rollover/financing data, no leverage

frozen_cost_stress_matrix.definition: round-trip cost in price basis points charged once per completed round trip: net_log_return = log(exit_open / entry_open) - cost_bps * 1e-4; proxy spread is a CONSERVATIVE STRESS INPUT, never a live-spread claim
frozen_cost_stress_matrix.one_event_delay_stress: every execution shifted one additional completed bar later; a delayed flatten that would land at/after the 15:00 NY boundary collapses into the 15:00 NY flatten fill, so the delay never violates the flat invariant
frozen_cost_stress_matrix.rationale: identical frozen matrix as FXFV1-A4-P1 (lane-level consistency); this mechanism trades nearly every day with no stop, so cost survival IS the primary scientific gate and is expected a priori to be the binding constraint

pair_universe.window: 2020-01-29 -> 2026-09-02 H1 canonical (approx 6.59y per pair), all 7 pairs evaluated identically
pair_universe.preregistered_heterogeneity_prediction: continuation should be strongest in the deepest-liquidity crosses (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) and weakest where Asian hours carry the information (USD/JPY on Japan-centric days); evaluated, not a kill rule

anchor.definition: R over London [08:00,11:00] completed bars (close-to-close from the 07:00 London stamp); enter sign(R) at the 12:00 London bar open; single mandatory exit at the 15:00 America/New_York bar open
anchor.why_it_validates: if FX intraday continuation is a session-structure phenomenon keyed to the London->NY information window, the threshold-free anchor should show positive net expectancy surviving the frozen cost matrix

neighbour.definition: single preregistered adjacent variant: signal window extended by one bar, R' = close(12:00 London) - close(07:00 London) (5 bars, stamps 08-12 London); entry fill at the 13:00 London bar open; exit unchanged (15:00 NY flatten)
neighbour.why_it_validates: one-bar adjacency: a real window-anchored flow phenomenon shifts smoothly; a data-snooped spike does not
neighbour.why_more_variants_are_forbidden: any additional window or filter level would be a grid; the neighbour is fixed here, before any returns exist

negative_control.definition: identical rule translated to the Tokyo session: R_t = close(bar stamped 12:00 JST) - close(bar stamped 08:00 JST) (4 completed bars, stamps 09-12 JST); entry fill at the 13:00 JST bar open; same single 15:00 NY flatten exit; Mondays structurally invalid (Mon 08:00 JST precedes the Sunday 21:00 NY weekly open)
negative_control.why_it_destroys: the claim is session timing: continuation lives in the London->NY window because that is when information diffuses and liquidity peaks. Tokyo midday is the documented FX activity trough (Andersen & Bollerslev 1997). If threshold-free continuation is equally strong in the trough, the anchor is generic daily momentum wearing a session story - the session-timing mechanism is destroyed and the anchor rejected
negative_control.causality_note: the control holds the rule, the threshold (none), the execution machinery and the exit constant, and moves only the session of signal formation and entry

falsification_rule.scope: evaluated only in the later authorized phase on the full canonical H1 window per pair; nothing here computes or inspects returns
falsification_rule.statistic_per_pair_per_arm: per-trade net log return (bps) under the stated stress cell; summary = mean trade expectancy with day-clustered t-stat, plus trade count

kills.V1_viability: FAIL if fewer than 4 of 7 pairs have mean net trade expectancy > 0 at stress x1.0/no-delay, OR fewer than 4 of 7 at x1.5/one-bar-delay
kills.V2_session_causality: FAIL if anchor mean net expectancy (x1.0/no-delay) does not exceed the Tokyo-control's in at least 5 of 7 pairs
kills.V3_neighbour_robustness: FAIL if Spearman rank correlation of anchor vs neighbour mean net expectancy across the 7 pairs is below +0.5
kills.V4_cost_fragility: FAIL if the sign of mean net expectancy differs between x1.0 and x2.0 in 5 or more pairs (stricter than P1's K4 because exposure here is near-continuous)

falsification_rule.survival_condition: V1 AND V2 AND V3 AND NOT V4 all hold; any other outcome falsifies the proposal as specified; no re-specification, no filter added, no window change permitted after any return is visible
falsification_rule.no_grid_search: the anchor has zero free parameters; the single neighbour is preregistered; no other configuration is evaluable under this proposal

expected_regimes.favours: high-liquidity trend days; macro-heavy mornings (08:30 NY releases inside the holding window); weeks when London and NY agree on direction
expected_regimes.adverse: range/consolidation weeks (morning move is the day's full excursion); risk-off illiquid episodes; holiday-thinned sessions; regimes where Asian hours carry the information (Japan-centric shocks)
expected_regimes.structural_bounds_not_results: threshold-free means approximately one trade per valid NY trading day (order of magnitude ~1300 trades/pair over 6.59y; Mondays valid for the anchor, invalid for the Tokyo control) - design bounds only, no returns computed here

dst_session_clock_spec.frozen_calendar: trading week Sunday 21:00 America/New_York open -> Friday 16:00 America/New_York close; daily rollover 17:00 America/New_York; all boundaries computed via zoneinfo named zones (DST-correct), matching DEFAULT_FX_WEEK_CONVENTION in research/assets/forex/sessions.py
dst_session_clock_spec.bar_labeling: each canonical H1 bar is labeled by its UTC open instant; London / Tokyo / NY wall-clock labels derived per bar via zoneinfo (Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo, America/New_York); UTC->zone mapping is single-valued so DST fall-back is unambiguous
dst_session_clock_spec.transition_days: US transitions occur ~02:00 local Sunday, UK transitions ~01:00 UTC Sunday: both outside all Mon-Fri windows used here, so no signal window or flatten boundary is ever truncated by a transition on a trading day
dst_session_clock_spec.flatten_boundary: 15:00 America/New_York wall-clock bar open (completion 16:00 NY), strictly before the 17:00 NY rollover by two full hours in both EST and EDT; during the ~2-3 weeks/year of US/UK DST desync the London-keyed entry drifts by one hour against NY, which zoneinfo handles exactly

data_fields_used: bar open timestamp (UTC) for session mapping via zoneinfo
data_fields_explicitly_not_used: twelvedata_h1_open/high/low beyond close-based signal (no range logic in this mechanism)
volume (null in canonical series; centralized FX volume forbidden)
any other provider, any fundamental/macro series

forbidden_assumptions_check.bid_ask_fabricated: PASS - proxy spread is a frozen stress input only, never an executable price
forbidden_assumptions_check.financing_or_swap_modeled: PASS - flat strictly before every rollover by construction; zero financing exposure
forbidden_assumptions_check.overnight_or_weekend_position: PASS - 15:00 NY flatten; Friday rule leaves the weekend flat
forbidden_assumptions_check.intrabar_fill_assumed: PASS - all fills at next allowed bar open
forbidden_assumptions_check.signals_on_incomplete_bars: PASS - signal computed only at the completion instant of the 11:00-London bar
forbidden_assumptions_check.grid_search_or_tuning: PASS - zero free anchor parameters (threshold-free by design), one preregistered neighbour, 21 fixed cells
forbidden_assumptions_check.outcome_peeking_or_old_proposal_rescue: PASS - outcome-blind; frozen research/proposals/forex/** not opened and not reused
forbidden_assumptions_check.beyond_authorized_data_contract: PASS - Twelve Data H1 OHLC, 7 pairs, 2020-01-29->2026-09-02 only

literature_sources.title: Market Intraday Momentum
literature_sources.authors: Lei Gao, Yufeng Han, Sophia Zhengzi Li, Guofu Zhou
literature_sources.claim: in US equities, the market's first half-hour return predicts its last half-hour return (intraday momentum)
literature_sources.verification: VERIFIED_METADATA (title/venue/finding via search; full text not re-read); established for US equity index futures, NOT for FX - the FX transfer is this proposal's hypothesis

literature_sources.title: Intraday Periodicity and Volatility Persistence in Financial Markets
literature_sources.claim: FX return volatility has a pervasive deterministic intraday periodicity keyed to the global session clock, peaking in the European/NY windows and troughing in Asian afternoon
literature_sources.verification: VERIFIED_METADATA (title/venue/finding via search; full text not re-read); motivates the anchor window and the placement of the Tokyo-midday negative control

literature_sources.title: Risk Everywhere: Modeling and Managing Volatility

literature_sources.claim: realized volatility measured from high-frequency data is strongly predictable at short horizons across global assets (intraday risk persistence)
literature_sources.verification: VERIFIED_METADATA (title/venue/finding via search); supporting context only: short-horizon persistence is the statistical backdrop for intraday continuation
